messages:
emily_support: FYI — AcmeProd reports streaming output that cuts off mid-JSON. No final finish_reason or terminal event. They see a trailing comma and parse errors on client side.

acme_support: Repro on our SDK v0.9.2 (node-fetch wrapper) — long response (~180 tokens) then auth token refresh happens in the middle, SDK reconnects with `X-Resume-Id` header, client receives partial JSON and no terminal event.

emily_support: Minimal repro steps they provided: 
1) Start SSE stream to /v1/streams?model=gpt-x with bearer token
2) After ~5s auth refresh fires (long-lived client flow) and SDK auto-reconnects
3) Reconnection includes `X-Resume-Id: <uuid>` header
4) Client parses stream, hits trailing comma / unterminated object, no `finish_reason` field anywhere

acme_support: snippet of raw frames they captured (sanitized):
```
data: {"id":1,"delta":"Hello"}

data: {"id":2,"delta":" world"}
...
data: {"id":180,"delta":"!"}

// client lost connection, reconnected with resume header

data: {"id":181,"delta":"more"}
...
// then stream ends abruptly, last chunk missing closing brace
```

dev_mike: thanks. Any proxies/cache between client and us (Fastly/nginx)?

acme_support: they go through a customer edge proxy + our infra. We saw a 401 from our auth server then client retry. No obvious 5xx from Redwood.

ingrid_sre: quick hypothesis: resume header swap is hitting a validation path -> our runtime is closing the connection without emitting final sentinel. I can see a code path where resume mismatch triggers a silent abort to avoid double-emit. That would explain missing finish_reason.

danielle_engineer: @ingrid_sre can you grep logs for `resume_mismatch` or `stream_closed_no_final` around ts 2943219800-2943220500? Also which model variant were they on?

ingrid_sre: found entries: 
```
WARN  runtime.resume: resume_header present but session_key mismatch (client_resume=abc123 expected=def456)
INFO  runtime.stream: stream_closed_no_final(session=abcd-efgh)
```

ingrid_sre: model: gpt-x-16k-qat (quantized), routed to pool `dedicated-03`.

dev_mike: ok, reproducer idea: issue a stream, kill auth token mid-stream, then reconnect with a mismatched resume header (simulate SDK bug). If we can reproduce locally, patch should be straightforward: emit an explicit final event with `{"finish_reason":"resume_mismatch"}` or send an error frame before closing.

emily_support: Customer would accept either an explicit error event or clear docs telling them to avoid resume on auth refresh. They hit production parsing errors.

acme_support: workaround deployed on their side: force SDK to do a full reconnect (new session) instead of resume. That fixes their parser errors but is obviously higher-cost.

dev_mike: short-term: add guard in runtime that if resume_header present but mismatch, we write a final SSE event: `data: {"finish_reason":"resume_mismatch","error":"resume header mismatch"}` and then close. Long-term: update resume protocol to validate resume IDs before relying on silent abort. I'll open ENG-5123.

ingrid_sre: I've flagged the tail-emit in logs and added an alert rule so we can detect future silent-closes.

sre-bot: Incident created ENG-5123 (streaming resume mismatch -> missing final event). Priority: P2. Assignees: dev_mike, ingrid_sre.

danielle_engineer: note for docs: call out that auth rotation SHOULD NOT reuse resume headers; SDKs must either carry forward session_key or start fresh. We'll draft a short note in the streaming docs.

emily_support: I'll update the customer thread with the workaround and ETA for patch. Thanks team :thumbsup:

acme_support: thanks — can we get a follow-up once patch is deployed? Their parsing errors are causing user-visible failures and billing noise (clients retrying).

dev_mike: will post a patch PR link and deployment ETA here. Targeting hotfix to runtime in the next 24-48h.

emily_support: adding this to the customer case; marking as escalated.
